newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Thursday sold steady to $0.50 per cwt lower amid limited demand following news Wednesday of deeper planned slaughter cutbacks, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at top prices of $58.50 to $59.00 in the country and $59.50 to $60.50 for hogs delivered to plants.
Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $59.50 to $60.00 in the country and $$60.50 to $61.00 at plants.
Indiana hogs sold $0.50 lower at $57.00 to $57.50 in the country and $60.00 to $60.50 at plants.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $57.50 to $58.00 in the country and $59.00 to $60.00 at plants, the dealers said.
IBP Inc on Wednesday announced it was trimming slaughter operations this week and next, due to poor profit margins. Several other major packers also reduced operations recently for the same reasons.
Cash hog prices also were pressured by increased hog marketings on Wednesday and outlooks for adequate movement Thursday, sources said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Wednesday totalled 104,000 head, above the 100,000 estimate, USDA said.
